title: Understanding Logistic Regression Output
text: In logistic regression, the output of the model is a probability that the given input belongs to a particular class. The sigmoid function is used to map any real-valued number into the range of $$0$$ to $$1$$.

title: Sigmoid Function
text: The sigmoid function, denoted as \( \sigma \), is defined as \( \sigma(z) $$=$$ \frac{1}{1+e**{-z}} \). It outputs a value between $$0$$ and $$1$$, which can be interpreted as a probability.

title: Probability of Sad Tweet
text: To find the probability that a tweet is sad, you need to compute \( P(Y=0|X=x_{test}) \). This is equivalent to \( $$1$$ - P(Y=1|X=x_{test}) \).

title: Computing Probability of Sad Tweet
text: Given the logistic regression model, the probability of a tweet being happy is \( \sigma(\theta**{T}x_{test}) \). Therefore, the probability of it being sad is \( $$1$$ - \sigma(\theta**{T}x_{test}) \).
